theater: 桑坦德灣與坎塔布里山區

battle.name: 坎塔布里戰爭
battle.theater: 桑坦德灣與坎塔布里山區
battle.brief: 前29年起，羅馬在伊比利亞北部對抗最後一批獨立的山地部族，戰火由桑坦德灣的造船營燒到貝爾諾里奧山巔，前19年以最後山寨陷落收場。卡面的羅馬方陣盾是這場戰爭真正的勝負手：它讓羅馬步兵在投射物密集的山地裡靠盾牆頂住坎塔布里人的拋石與標槍，再以短程突擊逐點拔掉山堡。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 坎塔布里戰爭（前29年—前19年）是羅馬共和國在奧古斯都治下，與伊比利亞北部坎塔布里、阿斯圖里亞諸部落聯盟之間的一場十年戰爭。戰場由比斯開灣南岸的桑坦德灣，向東穿過坎塔布里山脈，一直推到臨大西洋的北方岸線。開戰的是山地部族聯盟：坎塔布里人通常被說成由二十個部族組成，各有首領、據點與自己的徵召範圍，平日住村落與山堡，戰時以步兵戰士與輕裝游擊隊作戰，糧食靠田產、隨軍牛群與掠奪維持；同區的阿斯圖里亞人捲入戰事較深，卻一直保留較大的行動自由，直到前15年仍有另一場反亂。另一方是羅馬：最高指揮是執政官級的奧古斯都本人，其下是總督與副將分領的各路軍團，骨幹為第七「孿生」（Legio VII Gemina）、第十「孿生」（Legio X Gemina）與第六「勝凱」（Legio VI Victrix）等公民兵團，輔以高盧人、伊比利亞人編成的輔兵與騎兵，並有海軍分隊封鎖沿岸。第三種身分不是國家而是資源：阿斯圖里亞的金礦、坎塔布里銀礦與沿岸港口的商路，才是帝國真正想拿的東西。
countriesEn: The Cantabrian Wars (29-19 BC) were a ten-year conflict fought under Augustus by the Roman Republic against a confederation of Cantabrian and Asturian tribes in northern Hispania. The theatre ran from the Bay of Santander on the southern shore of the Bay of Biscay, eastward through the Cantabrian mountains, all the way to the Atlantic coast in the north. The side that opened the war was a mountain tribal confederation: the Cantabri are usually said to have comprised twenty tribes, each with its own leader, its own strongholds and its own levy, living in villages and hillforts in peacetime and fighting with infantry levies and light skirmishers in war, subsisting on their crops, the cattle that travelled with them and what they could take. The Asturians of the same region were drawn more deeply into the fighting yet kept a larger measure of independence, and another rising did not come until 15 BC. The other side was Rome: supreme command belonged to Augustus in his capacity of consul, and under him the provincial governor and several legates led separate columns. The backbone was the citizen legions - the seventh Gemini (Legio VII Gemina), the tenth Gemini (Legio X Gemina) and the sixth Victrix (Legio VI Victrix) among them - supported by auxiliaries and cavalry recruited among Gauls and Iberians, while a squadron of the fleet sealed off the coast. A third kind of party here is not a state but a resource: the gold of Asturias, the silver of Cantabria and the trade routes of the coastal ports were the things the empire truly wanted.
people: 這場戰爭的人事幾乎全部繞著奧古斯都轉。前29年，坎塔布里人夜襲海岸的羅馬造船營與軍務營地，殺死一名主持船塢的將官，戰端由此點燃；前28年奧古斯都親赴伊比利亞，收編前任總督留下的多路軍隊，改以集中兵力逐區推進，前27年回羅馬舉行小凱旋式後旋即再返戰場，前19年才收兵。替他管海路與補給的是馬庫斯·阿格里帕：北方部族曾自建艦隊在近海挑戰，被羅馬海軍擊退，阿格里帕是這條戰線的主導者。奧古斯都的姪子蓋烏斯·凱撒（前36年—前18年）在最後幾年於北方領軍，前18年卒於伊比利亞軍中，奧古斯都為之極度悲痛。敵方留下的名字有兩個最清楚：前22年在內陸擊潰總督馬庫斯·洛利烏斯、迫其沿海退走的因多；以及前19年拒絕投降、下令縱火焚燒營寨自守的那位坎塔布里女首領。斯特拉波另記了首領維利烏斯中計被誘入羅馬營地的經過。
peopleEn: The human story of this war turns almost entirely on Augustus. In 29 BC the Cantabri struck the Roman shipyard and administrative camp on the coast by night, killing the officer in charge of the naval works; that was the flash that lit the war. In 28 BC Augustus came to Hispania himself, took over the several columns left behind by his predecessors, and reorganised the campaign into a single advance carried out area by area; in 27 BC he returned to Rome for a lesser triumph (ovatio) and then went straight back to the front, and he only closed the war in 19 BC. Marcus Agrippa handled the sea route and the supply lines: the northern tribes had built a fleet of their own and challenged Roman control in coastal waters, and Agrippa was the man behind that front. Augustus' nephew Gaius Caesar (36-18 BC) commanded in the north during the closing years and died there in 18 BC, a blow Augustus bitterly mourned. Two names stand out on the other side. The first is Indo, who in 22 BC destroyed the governor Marcus Lollius in the interior and drove him back to the coast. The second is the Cantabrian chieftainess who refused to surrender in 19 BC and ordered her camp burned as a last act of defiance. Strabo also preserves the story of the leader Vellius, who was taken in by a ruse and led into the Roman camp.
kits: 卡面那面羅馬方陣盾（scutum）就是這場戰爭的技術核心。共和國晚期的方陣盾是直立微凸的長方木板，外蒙皮革，中央鑄鐵盾臍，高約一公尺、寬六七十公分，份量不輕，靠盾緣互相咬合成一整面盾牆。羅馬步兵在山地的每一場進攻都靠它：坎塔布里人從高處擲下石塊、標槍與投石索的彈丸，普通陣形撐不住，步兵便舉盾成龜甲（testudo）頂著落石推進，再以短兵相接的短程衝鋒奪下隘口；法比奧斯圍攻山堡時，盾牆同樣護住了推土、填壕與撞槍的作業組。羅馬的裝備清單還包括：皮爾姆式長矛與短劍、蒙福特諾式與新帝國高盧式青銅盔、鎖子甲與分段甲、由騾子牽引的車弩與配重投石器、攻城用的撞槍與土壘，以及每日扎下的野戰營制式與帳篷器材。坎塔布里人一側則是另一套：小圓盾（caetra）、帶弧刃的伊比利亞式彎刀與拉泰恩式長劍、長標槍與投石索、青銅盔與輕皮甲，他們以投石索手著稱，游擊時多不披甲。後期研究常引用出自貝爾諾里奧山堡的青銅女戰士像，那是當地工匠自行鑄造的奉納像，也是理解這一地區裝備樣貌最直接的物證。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card is the technical heart of this war. The Republican scutum was an upright, slightly convex rectangle of timber faced with leather, with a wrought-iron boss at the centre, roughly a metre tall and sixty to seventy centimetres wide, and heavy enough to be a burden; it was made to interlock edge to edge so that a rank of men became a single continuous wall. Every Roman advance in the mountains depended on it. The Cantabri hurled stones, javelins and sling-shot down from the heights, an ordinary formation could not absorb that, so the legionaries raised their shields into a testudo and pushed forward under the missiles, and only then broke through with a short-range rush to take the pass. When Fabius attacked the hillforts, the same shield wall covered the working parties who filled the ditch, raised the earthwork and worked the ram. The rest of the Roman equipment list runs to pila and short swords, Montefortino and new Imperial Gallic bronze helmets, chain and segmentata armour, mule-drawn carroballistae and stone-throwing engines, the battering ram and the siege earthwork, together with the kit and the formulae of the marching camp dug every evening. On the Cantabrian side the equipment was a different set: the small round caetra, Iberian curved blades and La Tène long swords, long spears and slings, bronze helmets and light leather armour, their slingers being famous and their skirmishers often fighting unarmoured. Later scholarship quotes the bronze figure of a warrior woman found in the hillfort of Monte Bernorio, cast by local craftsmen as a votive offering; it is the most direct physical evidence for what this region's gear looked like.
tactics: 兩邊的打法幾乎是互相定義的。坎塔布里人拒絕在平原上會戰，偏好利用石灰岩山地的峽谷、樹林與霧氣，遠距離以標槍與投石索消耗羅馬縱隊，再以輕裝騎兵掠過側翼，或在夜間燒掉羅馬的野戰營與糧隊；最後的據點是建在山脊上的石牆寨堡，牆後備足井水、柴薪與石塊，抵抗到最後才縱火自焚。羅馬的解法是三路並進：從北面海岸、從阿斯圖里亞山口、從東面梅里達方向同時施壓，把游擊戰拖成圍困戰；並在關鍵路口設永久軍營與軍港，冬季營地沿山麓一線排開，靠道路與船運維持糧食與飲水。奧古斯都還做了一件很有名的事：依斯特拉波的記載，他下令全軍模仿坎塔布里人的戰法，輕裝兵先鋒、重裝步兵居中、騎兵置於兩翼掩護，隊與隊之間留短暫休息，免得整縱隊在山地行軍中被拖散再遭襲擊。防線靠的仍然是方陣盾：盾緣相接的步兵線，加上龜甲隊形，這是羅馬在山地把裝備優勢換成推進力的方式。
tacticsEn: The two sides' ways of fighting are almost defined by each other. The Cantabri refused to give battle in the open, preferring to work the ravines, woods and fog of the limestone mountains, wearing down Roman columns at long range with javelins and sling-shot and then sweeping past their flanks with light cavalry, or burning the Roman camp and baggage train by night. Their last positions were stone-walled hillforts set on ridge-tops, with water, firewood and loose stone kept behind the walls, and they burned them only when there was nothing left to hold. Rome's answer was pressure from three directions at once: from the northern coast, from the Asturian passes and from the south-east around Mérida, which converted a war of raids into a war of siege. Permanent camps and a naval base were established at the key crossroads, winter quarters were laid out in a line along the foothills, and food and water were carried in on roads and by sea. Augustus also did something famous: according to Strabo he ordered the whole army to imitate the Cantabrian manner of fighting, with light troops in front, heavy infantry in the centre and cavalry on the wings, and with short rests between formations so that a column marching through the mountains was neither dragged out nor caught in the open. The line itself still rested on the scutum: the interlocking edge-to-edge shield wall, together with the testudo, was how Rome turned a material advantage into forward movement in the hills.
data: 這場戰爭的數字大半來自羅馬一方的記載，讀數時要留一分懷疑。狄奧說坎塔布里人大約有五十萬人口、二百個聚落，理論上能拉出二十萬步兵；這些都是羅馬人眼中蠻族的概數，實際能上陣的人數顯然遠低。羅馬方面常被認為投入三個軍團為主，加上輔兵與騎兵，兵員大致在二萬到三萬之間；前29年第一次深入山區即告失利，記載提到數百名羅馬兵被俘（其中被俘約八百的說法流傳最廣）。戰線本身不短：從桑坦德灣到貝爾諾里奧山約四十公里，羅馬軍隊沿阿斯圖加通往北海岸的山路行進，全程約一百二十公里以上，多半是海拔六百至一千四百公尺的谷地與隘口。戰爭打了十年、分三個階段：前29至前28年是開端，前25至前23年推進到山脈與大西洋岸，前22至前19年是壓榨式收尾。錢的數字也值得一記：普林尼估計阿斯圖里亞金礦的年產約兩萬磅黃金，坎塔布里沿岸銀礦（霍爾諾斯一帶）在羅馬接管後立刻成為財政收入。
dataEn: Most of the numbers for this war come from Roman sources and should be read with a degree of suspicion. Cassius Dio says the Cantabri had about five hundred thousand inhabitants and two hundred settlements and could theoretically raise two hundred thousand foot; these are Roman figures for a barbarian enemy, and the real number of men who could be put in the field was plainly far lower. Rome is generally thought to have committed three legions as its main effort, with auxiliaries and cavalry bringing the total to somewhere between twenty and thirty thousand men. The first deep push into the mountains in 29 BC ended in defeat, and the record speaks of several hundred Roman soldiers taken prisoner, a figure of about eight hundred prisoners being the version that circulated most widely. The frontage was not short either: some forty kilometres separate the Bay of Santander from Monte Bernorio, and the Roman columns travelled more than a hundred and twenty kilometres along the mountain road from Asturica to the northern coast, most of it through valleys and passes between six hundred and fourteen hundred metres above sea level. The war lasted ten years in three phases: an opening from 29 to 28 BC, the drive through the mountains to the Atlantic from 25 to 23 BC, and a grinding conclusion from 22 to 19 BC. The money is worth recording too: Pliny estimated the annual output of the Asturian gold mines at about twenty thousand pounds of gold, and the silver mines of the Cantabrian coast around Hornos became revenue for the Roman treasury as soon as they were taken over.
cause: 打起來的直接理由很具體：前29年坎塔布里人盯上了羅馬在比斯開灣南岸新修的造船營與軍港，殺死主持船塢的將官、燒掉船隻，把羅馬在北方的海岸基地打了個稀爛，羅馬以此為由出兵。但根子更深：公元前3世紀起，坎塔布里人就沿北岸反覆劫掠羅馬的殖民地與商站，羅馬因此沿海岸修起一串瞭望塔與營壘；進入前1世紀，羅馬需要一條能從內陸高原直通北方灣岸的軍用道路，也需要把銀礦收入國家口袋，而這些都還躺在坎塔布里人的山堡裡。同時，塞爾托里烏斯時代的盧西塔尼亞戰爭讓山地部族見識過羅馬的軟肋，前2世紀末以來坎塔布里人屢次趁邊境亂局出擊，使奧古斯都相信：只要北方的山地聯盟還保持獨立，整個伊比利亞的征服就不算完成。於是這場戰爭表面是報復，實際是帝國最後一次把邊界改寫成行省的工程。
causeEn: The immediate reason for the war was very concrete. In 29 BC the Cantabri went after the new Roman shipyard and naval base on the southern shore of the Bay of Biscay, killed the officer in charge of the works and burned the ships, wrecking Rome's coastal base in the north, and Rome used that as its casus belli. The roots go deeper. From the third century BC the Cantabri raided Roman colonies and trading stations along the northern coast again and again, and Rome answered by building a chain of watchtowers and camps along that shore. Onto the first century BC, Rome needed a military road running from the interior plateaux straight to the northern bay, and it needed the silver in the state treasury instead of in Cantabrian hands; both of those things still lay inside the hillforts. At the same time the Lusitanian war of the age of Sertorius had shown the mountain tribes where Rome was weak, and from the late second century BC the Cantabri struck again and again on the strength of trouble along the frontier, so that Augustus came to believe that as long as a mountain confederation in the north remained independent, the conquest of Hispania as a whole was not finished. So the war was revenge on the surface and, underneath, the empire's last conversion of a frontier into a province.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果改變的不只是北邊一條山脈。征服完成後，希斯帕尼亞從大洋到盧西塔尼亞海岸都進入奧古斯都的版圖，羅馬軍團沿北方邊境駐紮：第七「孿生」軍團以萊昂一帶的軍營為核心，阿斯圖里亞前線則以阿斯圖加為基地，前16年修通的跨山道路把山內城鎮與大西洋岸連成一線。伊比利亞的金銀自此源源流入帝國國庫，奧古斯都在《功業錄》中自稱已使從大洋到盧西塔尼亞海岸的西班牙獲得太平。北方的平靜維持了將近兩個世紀，直到公元2年與前15年阿斯圖里亞人先後再起反亂才被壓下去，最後一次由德魯蘇斯攻破山寨而終。文化層面的殘留也很有意思：坎塔布里這個名號沒有消失，晚期帝國的軍團名錄裡仍找得到以坎塔布里人編成的步兵營（cohors Cantabrorum），而貝爾諾里奧出土的青銅女戰士像，則成了這段歷史最常被引用的地方文物。
impactEn: What this war changed reached far beyond one mountain range in the north. Once the conquest was complete, all of Hispania from the ocean to the Lusitanian coast passed under Augustus, and Roman legions garrisoned the northern frontier: the seventh Gemini held the ground around its camp at León, the Asturian front was based on Asturica, and the road across the mountains, finished in 16 BC, tied the inland towns to the Atlantic shore in a single line. The gold and silver of Hispania began to flow into the imperial treasury without pause, and in the Res Gestae Augustus claimed that he had brought peace to all of Spain from the ocean to the coast of Lusitania. Peace in the north lasted close to two centuries, until Cantabrian and Asturian risings in AD 2 and in 15 BC were put down, the last of them when Drusus took a hillfort. The residue in cultural terms is remarkable as well: the name Cantabri did not vanish, and late imperial unit lists still carry infantry cohorts raised from Cantabri (cohors Cantabrorum), while the bronze figure of a warrior woman from Monte Bernorio has become the most frequently cited local artefact of this stretch of history.
result: 前19年，最後一批拒絕低頭的坎塔布里山寨在山中被攻破，殘餘的部族首領一個個出面議和，交出人質，部分首領之子被送往羅馬接受教育與人質式的管教；山區獨立的徵召權就此終止，坎塔布里一詞從對手變成邊民。對羅馬而言，這是一場打得乾淨卻漫長的戰爭：沒有真正的會戰勝負，只有十年間不斷推進、設營、築路、圍攻，最後以大家都已經同意收場。奧古斯都因此在政治上得利不淺，小凱旋式與隨後而來的行省指揮權都建立在北方這條山脈歸順之上；對後世史家而言，這場戰爭的真正意義是它替共和國的最後一段擴張畫上句號：從前3世紀到前1世紀，羅馬在伊比利亞打了兩百年，如今伊利斯帕尼亞成了帝國的穀倉、礦場與兵源庫，北方山民也從此被寫進了帝國的軍籍。
resultEn: In 19 BC the last Cantabrian hillforts that refused to bow were taken in the mountains, and the surviving tribal leaders came forward one by one to make terms, handing over hostages, with the sons of some chiefs sent to Rome to be educated and kept in a hostage manner. The independent levy of the uplands came to an end, and the word Cantabri changed from enemy to subject people. For Rome this was a war fought cleanly but slowly: there was no set-piece battle to decide it, only ten years of advance, encampment, road-building and siege, ending in a general agreement that everyone had come round. Augustus profited politically, and the lesser triumph and the proconsular imperium that followed rested on the submission of this northern range. For later historians the real significance is that the war closed the last chapter of Republican expansion: from the third century BC to the first, Rome had fought in Hispania for two hundred years, and now Hispania was the empire's granary, its mine and its recruiting ground, with the mountain folk of the north entered in the army lists.
